title: The Lord is my shepherd
hookLine: green pastures, still waters, the valley of the shadow (Psalm 23)
tomorrow: what does 'be still' mean when the whole world is shaking?

lines: SOFT LAMBS ON A GREETING CARD.
THE LAMB PULLED OUT OF ITS MOUTH.
cards: On a greeting card, shepherding looks gentle: soft lambs, green hills. The Bible's shepherd boy tells it differently.
Young David tells King Saul what he fought off to save one lamb, in the King James Version: "Thy servant kept his father's sheep, and there came a lion, and a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock."
He went after it, he says, and pulled the lamb out of its mouth.

teach.h: A SHEPHERD SINGS AS A SHEEP.
teach.b: Psalm 23 is headed a psalm of David. So the one who knows what a shepherd risks is now singing as a sheep: "The LORD is my shepherd."

teach.h: THE VALLEY: THOU ART WITH ME.
teach.b: Green pastures, still waters, and then the turn: "Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me." Today's question: who stays with you in the dark valley?
The psalm's answer isn't that the valley never comes. It's company. Thou art with me.
Many Jewish and Christian families read it at gravesides and hospital beds. It doesn't explain the dark; it walks through it beside you. Now a neighbor who shares the shepherd, in its own words.
In a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says God sent no prophet who did not herd sheep.

Asked about himself, he says yes, he herded them too, for the people of Mecca. Shared: the shepherd as the picture of care, learned with a flock before it's given to people. And the honest difference.
In Psalm 23, the LORD is the shepherd and the singer is the sheep. In the hadith, the prophets are the shepherds, trained by flocks to care for people. One image, held from two sides.

how: Jews and Christians pray Psalm 23 at funerals, at bedsides and in daily prayer; in some Jewish homes it is sung at the third Sabbath meal. Muslims honor the prophets, including David (Dawud) and Muhammad, as shepherds who herded sheep.

games.q: what does “the lord is my shepherd” mean?
o: God as a shepherd who stays close in the dark
a farmer's prayer for good weather and grass
a king's song about winning a great battle

games.q: one shepherd, two houses: tap the pairs.
p: fought a lion and a bear for a lamb
God as shepherd, or prophets as shepherds

s: Psalm 23 promises the dark valley will never come
it walks into the valley; the promise is company: thou art with me.
in a hadith, the Prophet Muhammad says he herded sheep too
God sent no prophet who did not herd sheep, and he had herded them for the people of Mecca.
shepherding in the Bible was soft, safe work
David told Saul he went after a lion and a bear to save one lamb.

games.q: a lion has taken a lamb from your father's flock. you're young David with a staff and a sling. what does the text say you did?
o: let the one lamb go to keep the rest of the flock safe.
ran back to the village for the men to help.
went after it and pulled the lamb out of its mouth.
games.why: he went after the lion and delivered the lamb out of its mouth. the singer of Psalm 23 knew what a shepherd risks.

practice: Read the whole psalm once, slowly, from any Bible or a screen, aloud if you can. If it isn't near, say verse four slowly: "Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me."
Then let the words settle like water going still.

wordCard.voice: The Lord is my shepherd: the first line of Psalm 23, sung by a shepherd as a sheep, with company promised in the valley.

carryVoice: Keep this one: still waters, and someone walking beside you to them. Three psalms in, and the valley isn't empty.
